chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) would seek refuge every day from six characteristics: doubt, associating partners with God, undue bias, anger, transgression, and jealousy.

key_terms.وَالْحَمِيَّةِ: Undue bias or pride (often referring to tribal or personal arrogance)

ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics the Prophet sought refuge from daily?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) consistent spiritual discipline in seeking protection from six specific vices, linking inner purification to prophetic example. The inclusion of *hamiyyah* (tribal pride or bias) and *bughy* (transgression) reflects key ethical concerns in Shia jurisprudence and theology, emphasizing the transition from individual piety to communal justice. This practice serves as a foundational model for *tazkiyah* (self-purification), encouraging believers to internalize these traits as daily spiritual diagnostics.
